# Terra provider-error diagnosis — 2026-11-13

Diagnosis only: no application/test/SDK changes, no new model requests. Read existing Q02/Q07 observations, inspected the installed SDK, reconstructed requests through HTTP MockTransport and checked strict-schema requirements locally. Sources and harness remain unchanged.

## Confirmed findings

Both historical failures are Terra `evaluate_candidates` generations with `BadRequestResponseError: Provider returned error`. No evidence completion exists. Available Langfuse metadata contains the same short error; original provider body, provider name and `error.metadata.raw` were not archived. Therefore the precise historical upstream rejection cannot be quoted or proved from these records.

**A concrete request-side schema defect is confirmed.** We send `response_format.type=json_schema`, `strict=true`, `provider.require_parameters=true`, `reasoning.effort=medium`, `max_tokens=8192`, model `openai/gpt-6.1-terra`. In both `character.items` and `individual_compatibility.items`, `observation_external_id` is a nullable property with a default, but is absent from `required`.

For OpenAI strict structured output all declared properties must be required; optional business values are represented by nullable required fields. See [OpenAI strict schema requirements](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/structured-outputs?api-mode=chat) and [OpenRouter's provider comparison](https://openrouter.ai/blog/tutorials/structured-output-llm/). The current request violates this requirement. This is the strongest explanation for the Terra rejection; it remains a diagnosis rather than a recovered historical provider message.

Installed `langchain-openrouter` 0.2.9 calls `convert_to_json_schema(schema)` without forwarding `strict` in its JSON-schema path, then sets strict on the outer response format. Installed `langchain-core` 1.7.6 already has a strict conversion path. Offline comparison confirms `convert_to_json_schema(CandidateEvidence, strict=True)` fills the missing required entries. This does not prove all provider compatibility or server acceptance, and does not constitute a code fix.

The same adapter issue affects `GroundingResponse`: `question_coverage.issues`, and issue fields `atom_id`, `fragment_id`, `quote`, are not all required in the current strict wire schema. This could contribute to Luna provider failures too, but those historical errors are not causally established either. A successful call through one route does not validate the schema against every provider route.

| Q02 | 2 | 7 | 6450 |
| Q07 | 1 | 2 | 4639 |

Both requests contain two messages: system extraction instructions and a user JSON payload with `character_criteria`, `candidate_sources`, and `compatibility_targets`. Character criterion: the exact `quiet home` quote with its criterion/fragment IDs. Sources include biography/profile/encyclopedia labels, candidate IDs and original text. There are no observation source records in these two specific requests; the invalid observation field still belongs to the requested output schema. This is not an eleven-card evidence request: the evidence step receives the selected shortlist. No evidence of context-window exhaustion was found in these small requests; it is not the established failure cause.

Langfuse deduplicates previously logged text into source references. The offline reconstruction expands the one biography reference in each request from its exact referenced tool observation; those dictionaries are telemetry representation, not text sent to the model. Headers/credentials are not archived. These are reconstructed requests using preserved messages and unchanged SDK/settings, **not original captured historical HTTP bodies**. Mock responses are local fixtures and are not model outputs or real provider errors.

## Why the exact error is lost

The OpenRouter SDK error object retains `status_code`, `body`, `raw_response` and structured error data, but its `__str__` returns only the short message. Our trace error projection records the exception type and first 300 characters of `str(error)`, so useful provider details are lost. The unhandled evidence exception becomes application HTTP 500; the live runner then attempts JSON parsing of the non-JSON body and records `JSONDecodeError`, masking the original error in its top-level record. Langfuse recovers the SDK class/stage but not the discarded raw body.

[OpenRouter error documentation](https://openrouter.ai/docs/api_reference/errors-and-debugging) describes provider metadata fields; the current short status message is insufficient to identify which schema field or provider rejected the request.

## Recommended next change, not implemented

1. Normalize provider-facing strict schemas, including nested required/nullability, while preserving typed Python response validation and observation-ID checks. Cover actual SDK-generated request JSON with an offline transport test.
2. Preserve allowlisted provider error fields (status, code, provider name, raw error details) in telemetry; preserve the HTTP failure body in evaluation archives rather than replacing it with JSONDecodeError.
3. Only after these local checks, explicitly authorize a small paid confirmation run. No automatic retries or inference calls were made during this diagnosis.
